overview: Armenia is a landlocked country in the South Caucasus, where Europe meets Asia. Its capital and largest city is Yerevan, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. In the early 300s Armenia became the first country to adopt Christianity as its official religion. It became independent from the Soviet Union in 1991, and the Armenian language has its own unique alphabet.

geography.text: Armenia is a mountainous country, and most of it lies more than 1,000 metres above sea level. Lake Sevan, one of the largest high-altitude freshwater lakes in the world, lies in the east. Mount Ararat, a national symbol that can be seen from Yerevan, stands just across the border in Türkiye.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Hot, dry summers and cold, snowy winters on a high plateau.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: The rare Caucasian leopard and the Armenian mouflon live in the mountains.

history.text: Armenia is one of the oldest nations in the world, and in 301 it became the first state to adopt Christianity. Its lands were later fought over by the Persian, Ottoman and Russian empires. During the First World War, between 600,000 and 1.5 million Armenians were killed in the genocide carried out by the Ottoman government. Armenia became independent in 1991.

events.title: Christian kingdom
events.text: Armenia becomes the first state to adopt Christianity.

events.title: Armenian alphabet
events.text: Mesrop Mashtots creates the Armenian alphabet.

events.title: Armenian Genocide
events.text: The Ottoman government begins the mass killing and deportation of Armenians.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Armenia becomes independent from the Soviet Union.

events.title: Nagorno-Karabakh
events.text: Azerbaijan takes full control of the region and its Armenian population flees.

government.text: Armenia is a parliamentary republic. The National Assembly chooses the Prime Minister, who leads the government, and elects the President, whose role is mostly ceremonial. In 2018 peaceful street protests, called the Velvet Revolution, brought a new government to power.

economy.text: Armenia's economy includes mining (especially copper), brandy, IT and tourism. Many Armenians live abroad, and money from the diaspora is important. The economy grew quickly after 2022 as many Russians and businesses moved there.

culture.text: Armenia has its own alphabet, created in 405, and its own branch of Christianity, the Armenian Apostolic Church. Mount Ararat, the mountain where Noah's Ark is said to have landed, is a national symbol though it lies in Türkiye. Lavash, a thin flatbread, is on UNESCO's heritage list.

items.title: Lavash
items.text: Thin bread baked in a clay oven, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Geghard Monastery
items.text: Partly carved out of a mountain cliff.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Lavash flatbread, khorovats barbecue and dolma, stuffed vine leaves.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: The duduk, a woodwind instrument made from apricot wood, has a haunting sound listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: On Vardavar, a summer festival, people throw water at each other in the streets.

sport.text: Chess is compulsory in Armenian schools, and Armenia's men's team won the Chess Olympiad three times. Weightlifting and wrestling have brought Olympic medals, and Henrikh Mkhitaryan is the country's best-known footballer.

items.title: Henrikh Mkhitaryan
items.text: Has played for Manchester United, Arsenal and Inter Milan.

didYouKnow: Armenia was the first country to make Christianity its state religion, in 301.
Chess is a compulsory subject in Armenian primary schools.
